issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a Rideable.messageOnRide() method with no parameters (returns a String like "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"), and the template's Main invokes r.messageOnRide() with no arguments. However, the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and implements it accordingly in Pig and Seal. This method-parameter mismatch makes the solution incompatible with the specification and the template usage and would confuse students about the required signature and return format.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Rideable interface and its implementations with the problem statement and template: change Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) to messageOnRide() returning String, and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, if an equipment parameter is intended, update the problem statement and template (including Main) to document and use the parameter consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement UML and the template Main expect a no-argument method messageOnRide(): String (Rideable.messageOnRide()). The solution repository changes the method signature to messageOnRide(String equipment), adding a parameter called 'equipment'. This creates a mismatch: student code in the template (Main) calls r.messageOnRide() with no argument and the UML specifies no parameter, but the solution API requires an argument. This breaks the conceptual mapping between the UML/problem description, the starter code, and the provided solution and will cause compilation/runtime confusion for students.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across all artifacts. Either revert the solution's Rideable.messageOnRide to a no-argument method (messageOnRide()) and update Pig/Seal implementations accordingly, or update the problem statement and template Main to require and use the new parameter (e.g., call messageOnRide("<equipment>")). Prefer restoring the no-arg signature to match the UML and starter Main code.
